open_questions: Wide TESS binary at true 2.51d with spot-induced depth modulation can mimic odd/even, needs RV to test
dossier.public_summary: The dip looks planetary but odd transits are much deeper than even ones and the depth jumps 25-fold between TESS sectors and between individual transits. The star also shows strong spot variability. Together this matches a stellar eclipse or blended variable star, not a stable planet, so the signal is rejected.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ strongly, with odds about 1.5x deeper than evens, consistent with a binary at twice the period rather than a planet.

Depth changes by a factor of 25 between sectors and transit_depths chi2 27948.84 dof 18 p_consistent 0.0 show extreme transit-to-transit variation (top three share 0.408 with outliers 122k-127k ppm), positive evidence against a stable planet.
